name: Super-Kamiokande
summary: Large water-Cherenkov neutrino experiment that also searches for neutrinos from dark-matter annihilation and scattering of dark matter boosted by cosmic rays.
detection_principle: Measures Cherenkov rings produced in water by electrons, muons or visible protons, using energy, topology and direction to seek excesses above atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: Kamioka's official historical table lists Super-K as running from 1996 to the present; an independent 2026 dark-matter-analysis status has not been verified.

collaboration.name: Super-Kamiokande collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

phases.name: SK-I—IV
phases.description: Phase used in the published boosted-DM search

phases.name: SK-Gd
phases.description: Subsequent gadolinium-loaded water upgrade; individual search results follow their papers

results.summary: The proton-recoil search found no significant excess toward the Galactic center.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
